The scope and criteria of its verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” appended to the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example and upholds the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to follow. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 with a view to achieving fully green mobility. The HKMA continues to incorporate environmental considerations into the design, operation, repair and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in various renovation projects undertaken in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in its offices and data centres. As part of a data centre facilities upgrade project in 2024, it adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply system to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design enables flexible capacity expansion, enhances operating efficiency under partial loads, and incorporates advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA strengthens internal virtual collaboration through its digital workplace and streamlines workflows, effectively reducing paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices with reference to manufacturers’ software update cycles, thereby extending the period during which the devices can be used securely. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the “4R” principles of refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are placed at convenient locations throughout the HKMA’s offices. To increase the recycling rate, the HKMA added collection bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit nets in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department’s “Waste Reduction Pledge for Events”, pledging to take measures to reduce waste generated by various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of products that meet the environmental specifications in the Government’s Green Procurement List, particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their itineraries carefully, such as by combining multiple trips wherever possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing approximately 10% of its annual carbon emissions from air travel. In addition, the HKMA participates in Gold Standard-certified carbon offset programmes to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel. These programmes focus on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to deepen their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 throughout May, the HKMA held its first “HKMA Green Month” under the theme “Think Green, Live Green, Work Green”. This provided an excellent opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to and momentum in embedding environmental sustainability into its internal operations. The programme included a “Sustainability BINGO Scorecard” encouraging staff to practise green living, a “Save the Earth” quiz, and a workshop on caring for kokedama, an indoor plant arrangement originating in Japan. The results of the waste audit were also shared, and an operator of community recycling centres introduced best recycling practices. To sustain the momentum of Green Month, the HKMA launched an approximately six-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that collectively making small changes to individual habits can significantly improve the organisation’s overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of the “Green ‘Fit’ Actions” video, in which senior executives shared recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic reminders encouraging staff to lead by example in reducing waste and increasing recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability and collect their views on proposed green workplace initiatives. The findings will help inform future sustainability training activities and waste disposal strategies. As Hong Kong’s central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as an important agent of change and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable operating practices across the financial sector and wider community. The HKMA has introduced various measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the Common Data Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform’s service coverage in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, facilitating their submission of certain regulatory information. The expansion aims to further streamline submission processes for reporting institutions and provide a smoother experience for all users, while reinforcing the HKMA’s commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 included SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA surveys through a streamlined submission process, and the Intelligent Information and Document Management System, a centralised platform providing users with advanced search capabilities for bank-related documents.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the “Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), GHG emissions from air travel, and their respective intensities for 2024. In addition, the Data include Scope 3 GHG emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting, as well as their respective intensities, for 2023 and 2024. The HKMA’s GHG emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covered a total of six office and warehouse premises, comprising five offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the six premises. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information”, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion at a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was established in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The completeness and accuracy of the Data were tested by tracing selected sample data back to their sources. The underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking were also reviewed and tested for reliability. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was conducted with complete independence and impartiality. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the preparation of the Data. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - the Data are materially accurate and reliable; - the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Siu-yan Shum Audit Manager Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
